summary: A shell terminal in iDrive: run commands on the head unit from the car's screen
author: Joseph Robinson
description:
ID6Term adds a Terminal row under Vehicle Apps in the ConnectedDrive menu of an NBT Evo (iDrive 6) head unit. From there you type a command line with the iDrive speller and run it through the head unit's /bin/sh; the output shows in a scrollable console screen. No SSH cable, no laptop: the car's own screen and controller.

What it does
- One long-lived shell session, like a terminal: cd, variables, functions and background jobs carry over from one command to the next
- Speller input with suggestions from your history and eight quick commands (uname -a, pidin arg, ifconfig, df, ls -la /, ...)
- Output streamed into the console while a command runs; Stop interrupts a command like Ctrl-C; a 20 s timeout per command (configurable)
- Built-ins: clear, help, history, kbd (letter case of the on-screen keyboard)

What you need
- An NBT Evo head unit with iDrive 6 (ID6). Car-tested on an NBT Evo (the Vehicle Apps placement is new in this version)
- NBTApps agent 1.2.0 or later

After installing
The iDrive screen restarts. Open ConnectedDrive and choose Terminal under Vehicle Apps.

What it places and writes
- The plugin goes into the HMI's plugin folder as ID6Term (libID6Term.so, ID6Term.manifest, ID6Term.xml and the text/image DBs). Nothing of the head unit's own software is replaced
- At run time it keeps your command history, keyboard mode and an optional config in /var/opt/id6term (or /dev/shmem when /var/opt is not writable), and a log at /dev/shmem/id6term-app.log, which NBTApps can fetch. Removing the package leaves /var/opt/id6term in place
- Plugin ids: connector 300, entry focus 32760

Good to know
- Commands run on the head unit as the HMI's user (root). A wrong rm, a renamed system file or a hung process can leave the unit unbootable, and only a reflash recovers it. There is no undo: use it at your own risk
- stdin of every command is /dev/null, so nothing here is interactive
- If ID6Term was put on this car by hand before (install.sh from its repo), run its uninstall.sh first: NBTApps refuses to write over files that no package placed
- The on-screen keyboard opens in upper case; the app folds letters to lower case by default (the kbd built-in changes that)
